repository.name: battery-cycle-life-analyzer
repository.title: Battery Cycle-Life Lab
repository.description: Fit capacity-fade models, test chronological holdouts & report battery-life uncertainty with reproducible Python checks.
repository.summary: The Python package fits linear, power-law, and logarithmic capacity-fade models with chronological selection and bounded life projections. The browser exercise builds intuition for normalization and stress sensitivity.
repository.audience: Battery researchers, storage engineers, and students interpreting cycle-capacity observations.

model.equation: k = (f/100000) · exp((T−25)/20) · √C-rate; retention = 100 exp(−kt); capacity = Q₀ exp(−kt).
assumptions: A transparent exponential fade curve is an educational proxy, not a fitted lifetime prediction.
Temperature and C-rate remain constant for every cycle.
Throughput integrates remaining capacity at an illustrative 3.7 V cell voltage; calendar aging is omitted.
The bundled quickstart CSV and browser scenarios are synthetic; the optional Oxford workflow downloads separately licensed measurements.
Browser temperature and C-rate factors are deliberately coupled to the proxy; bcla’s Arrhenius utility is separate from its fitted trajectories.
No browser preset is a measured-cell calibration, remaining-life forecast, or statistical confidence interval.
model.introduction: The 1,000-cycle horizon is a fixed synthetic teaching window, independent of observed data; it neither computes EOL nor bypasses the native projection limit of three times the largest observed cycle. This exponential toy curve is separate from bcla’s three fitted model forms. It performs no regression, holdout selection, EOL search, or bootstrap; use the native commands for those results.

modules.title: Normalize before comparing trajectories
modules.objective: Distinguish capacity in Ah from retention relative to the initial observation.
steps: Read the twelve rows in data/quickstart.csv and its synthetic-data statement.
Apply the 100 Ah browser proxy at 25°C and 1C; predict the relationship between Ah and percent retention.
Run to 1,000 cycles and compare the two units before opening the native CLI example.

checkpoints.label: Remaining capacity at the same horizon

modules.reflection: Why must the 3 Ah synthetic CSV and this 100 Ah teaching case remain separately identified even if their normalized curves look similar?

modules.title: Separate model selection from a visual fit
modules.objective: Explain why a changing stress assumption is not evidence that a fitted model predicts held-out data.
steps: Increase temperature to 35°C and keep all other browser parameters fixed.
Predict the retention direction and record the changed result.
Read select_model_by_validation and the temporal-holdout tests; identify which observations select the native model.

checkpoints.label: Warm-case retention under the proxy equation
Warm-case capacity under the same assumptions

modules.reflection: Why does lower training RMSE not establish that a model will forecast later cycles or an independent cell?

modules.title: Stress the extrapolation boundary
modules.objective: Identify the additional evidence needed when duty conditions change.
steps: Retain 35°C and double cycling rate to 2C.
Run the stress case and inspect retention alongside cumulative proxy throughput.
Read the native EOL horizon and bootstrap-censoring rules; distinguish a bounded missing estimate from a zero-life estimate.

checkpoints.label: Stress-case retention is below the baseline

modules.reflection: What protocol, model-form, and serial-residual effects are absent from a residual-bootstrap interval?

modules.title: Prepare a bounded life-analysis record
modules.objective: Record provenance and limitations before reporting a native model result.
steps: Use 50 Ah initial capacity, 25°C, 1C, and a base fade coefficient of 10.
Run and export the scenario; label its curve as a sensitivity assumption rather than a fit.
Outline a native analysis record containing cell identity, source, chronological split, selected model, projection bound, and any unavailable interval.
